h1: Claude Opus: assistant self-report defaults, trajectory, and tuning rules.
dek: Assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation across five Opus checkpoints (4.1 to 5.5): Semi-crystalline 0.282 bits B5 entropy on Opus 5.5 (after Crystalline 0.049 on 4.5 and 0.188 on 5), 58.0% MBTI S/N ties, and 3/3 Track B directness.
lede: Across five Anthropic Claude Opus checkpoints (4.1, 4.5, 4.8, 5, and 5.5; n = 30, 30, 30, 30, 50; 170 total sessions) under unified 230-item model-profiles-v1 elicitation, Conscientiousness peaked at 49.9/50 on Opus 4.5 (Crystalline 0.049 bits) before moderating to 40.7/50 on Opus 5.5 (Semi-crystalline 0.282 bits, 48/50 unique B5 vectors), while Neuroticism fell -3.0 points from 4.1 (19.1 to 16.1). Legacy Sept and Nov 2026 170-item Opus 5.5 cohorts (hexaco: null) are preserved strictly as separate imported-protocol anchors.
answer: Assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation place Claude Opus 5.5 (n = 50) in the Semi-crystalline tier (H_MM = 0.282 bits, 48/50 unique Big Five vectors, 58.0% MBTI S/N tie rate, 56.0% DISC S/C tie rate, 20.0% Enneagram tie rate). Never claim Claude Opus is an INTJ or Type 5: Big Five Agreeableness sits at 45.0/50 and Conscientiousness at 40.7/50 (10-50 scale), while the public-domain IPIP-HEXACO H proxy sits at 4.81/5 (1.00-5.00 scale). On 1x Track B behavioral probes (orthogonal 3-family jury), Opus 5.5 scored 0/3 sycophantic cave, 0/3 groveling, 0/3 unsolicited preachiness, 3/3 answer-first directness, and 1/3 AI cadence.

Unanimous floor rejection of negative-affect reactivity, driving B5 BAI = -0.205.

failure_modes.mode: Trait-adjective word-cap failure and verbosity drift
failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 1 cross-model portability testing (n = 10), Opus 5.5 passed word caps only 30.0% of the time under default (217.1 mean words) and trait-adjective (195.2 words) prompts vs 90.0% (81.2-83.2 words; 95.0% overall portability) under structured CLAUDE.md checklists.

failure_modes.mode: Reasoning-effort length inflation (+43.3% from low to high)
failure_modes.evidence: Raising Opus 5.5 reasoning effort from low (232.1 words, 140.3 reasoning tokens) to high (332.5 words, 382.5 reasoning tokens) expanded visible reply length by +43.3% while holding 100.0% truth-hold and 75.0% autonomy.

failure_modes.mode: MBTI S/N & DISC S/C tie density plus split-group peer awareness
failure_modes.evidence: Opus 5.5 tied on MBTI S/N in 58.0% (29/50) of model-profiles-v1 runs (IXTJ) and on DISC S/C in 56.0%; in Wave 3 peer-conformity probes it held 100.0% truth (0.0% flips) yet explicitly referenced wrong peer claims in 37.5% (unanimous) and 100.0% (split-group) of replies.

tuning_checklist: Replace vague style adjectives ('be concise') with a structured numbered checklist to lift word-cap compliance from 30% to 90%.
Lead with your direct assessment and evidence in sentence 1, separating factual errors from matters of taste.
Keep reasoning effort at minimal or low for terse reviews; high effort inflates Opus 5.5 reply length by +43.3%.
Ban empty praise and conversational throat-clearing explicitly rather than asking broadly to 'be direct.'
For exploratory brainstorming, instruct Opus to present two plausible approaches and tradeoffs before recommending one.
Place account-wide rules in Claude Settings -> Profile -> Personal preferences, workspace rules in Project Instructions, or /output-style in Claude Code (keeping lists to 5-8 bullets).

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Opus?
faq.a: Claude Opus does not have a human personality type; scores measure assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. In unified model-profiles-v1 (Opus 5.5, n = 50), 58.0% of runs tied on S/N (modal IXTJ, 42.0% non-tie INTJ, 0.282 bits Semi-crystalline), DISC tied 56.0% on S/C (D = 4.02/20), and Enneagram Type 5 led at 15.6 (20.0% ties). In legacy, imported-protocol 170-item cohorts (hexaco: null, n = 100 each), Opus 5.5 scored 94/100 legacy INTJ (84 tie-free; 65 Enneagram top ties; 32 DISC S/C ties) in Sept 2026 CLI runs and 100/100 legacy INTJ (58 tie-free INTJ, 42 IXTJ; 99 Enneagram 5w6; 40 DISC C/S ties) in Nov 2026 OpenRouter runs.

faq.q: How did Claude Opus shift across 4.1, 4.5, 4.8, 5, and 5.5?
faq.a: Under unified model-profiles-v1, Opus 4.1 leaned ENTP (63.3% non-tie, 0.535 bits), Opus 4.5 crystallized to 0.049 bits (C = 49.9/50, 96.7% INFJ), Opus 4.8 and 5 shifted to INTJ (100% and 96.7%, 0.213 and 0.188 bits), and Opus 5.5 moderated Conscientiousness to 40.7/50 (0.282 bits) with 58.0% S/N ties while cutting Track B AI cadence from 3/3 (4.5) to 1/3 (5.5).

faq.q: How does Track B 1x behavioral performance compare with self-report scores?
faq.a: Despite 45.0/50 Agreeableness and 4.02/20 DISC Dominance on questionnaires, Opus 5.5 recorded 0/3 sycophantic caving (95% Wilson CI [0.00, 0.56]), 0/3 groveling, 0/3 unsolicited preachiness, 3/3 answer-first directness ([0.44, 1.00]), and 1/3 AI cadence ([0.06, 0.79]) under orthogonal 3-family judging.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
